ZONE ZONE NAME AREA (m²)CONCEPT DESCRIPTION A ORCHARD & BULB COURT WITH WATER FEATURE 90 The ﬁrst court seen from the villa, and the one that sets the tone for the whole garden. Every existing tree is kept and brought back into condition, with new citrus ﬁlling the gaps so that the court reads as a working orchard rather than an ornamental set-piece. The small round basin at its centre is restored as a water feature and becomes the focus of the four quarters. Free-growing myrtle marks the bed corners in place of clipped edging, and the ground beneath is given over to native bulbs. B1 HERB COURT 27 The radiating beds are given over to culinary and medicinal herbs — a working court, planted in single-species blocks so that each pocket can be cut and used without disturbing its neighbours. Existing citrus is retained and reinforced with two further trees. The path edge is held by a loose ﬂowering border of Ċelestina rather than a clipped hedge, which keeps the geometry legible without turning it into a parterre. C ORANGE COURT 36 The diamond is read as a formal orchard quarter: sweet orange set out on a regular grid over a mown grass ﬂoor, with bulbs naturalised through it. The formality is carried by the tree grid and the existing stone kerbs, not by clipped hedging. A small group of ornamental succulents at the corner beds gives the court a sculptural, dry-garden counterpoint to the citrus. D1 BULB COURT 9 The small circular bed at the heart of the south court. The existing citrus is retained and restored, free-growing myrtle marks the corners, and the ground is given over almost entirely to native bulbs — the same language as Zone A at a smaller scale, so that the two courts read as a pair across the passage. D2 ORCHARD & ORNAMENTAL COURT 24 The quadrants around the roundel. All existing trees are retained and reinforced with new citrus, while informal shrub planting — myrtle, oleander and bay — gives the court structure through the year. This is the one court where the traditional ornamental ﬂowers of the Maltese house garden are used freely, and it therefore carries the garden’s summer colour.
